At Amazon, our tech isn't just a tool, it's your playground. Our engineers work on scalable systems, cloud services, and customer-facing products that operate at global scale. **About The Team**
Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon at Amazon - including Graviton (our server processors), Trainium and Inferentia (our machine learning training and inference accelerators), and the Nitro system that powers modern EC2. We own the full stack, from silicon through the software that makes it work (compilers, runtimes, drivers, and the frameworks that let customers run workloads on our hardware). As a Software Development Engineer I, you'll write the software that turns custom silicon into products used by millions.
  
  
**Where You Might Land**
Annapurna has software teams spanning the full stack, and we work to place you on a technical team aligned with your interests and strengths. Example teams and focus areas include:
  
  

* Compiler development for ML accelerators (Neuron SDK, MLIR, LLVM)
* ML runtimes and frameworks (integration with PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow)
* Low-level systems software, firmware, and device drivers
* Performance optimization and kernel development for custom silicon
* Distributed training and inference infrastructure

Once you join, we partner with you and our hiring managers to match you to a team where your background and interests fit best, so your project is something you're genuinely excited to work on.
  
  
As an SDE I, you'll contribute to real production software, which may include:
  
  

* Designing, implementing, and testing software across the stack - from low-level systems code to compilers, runtimes, and tooling
* Writing efficient, maintainable code in languages such as C, C++, or Python
* Optimizing software performance on custom hardware (Graviton, Trainium, Inferentia)
* Debugging complex issues across the hardware-software boundary
* Collaborating with hardware, compiler, and systems teams to deliver features end-to-end
* Documenting your work and presenting results to the team

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree program in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, with a final graduation date of May 2027 or later
* Programming experience in at least one modern language such as C, C++, Java, or Python
* Coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, and software design
* Understanding of core computer science fundamentals: operating systems, computer architecture, or systems programming

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree with a focus on systems, compilers, computer architecture, or high-performance computing
* Experience with low-level or systems programming in C/C++ (memory management, concurrency, performance optimization)
* Familiarity with compilers (MLIR, LLVM, TVM), ML runtimes, operating systems internals, or distributed systems
* Exposure to machine learning frameworks and an understanding of how models run on hardware
* Prior internship, research, or open-source contribution experience in systems, compilers, or ML infrastructure

**Overview**
Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center is an independent, nonprofit organization providing adult cancer treatment and groundbreaking research focused on cancer and infectious diseases. Based in Seattle, Fred Hutch is the only National Cancer Institute-designated cancer center in Washington.
  
  
With a track record of global leadership in bone marrow transplantation, HIV/AIDS prevention, immunotherapy and COVID-19 vaccines, Fred Hutch has earned a reputation as one of the world’s leading cancer, infectious disease and biomedical research centers. Fred Hutch operates eight clinical care sites that provide medical oncology, infusion, radiation, proton therapy and related services, and network affiliations with hospitals in five states. Together, our fully integrated research and clinical care teams seek to discover new cures to the world’s deadliest diseases and make life beyond cancer a reality.
  
  
At Fred Hutch we value collaboration, compassion, determination, excellence, innovation, integrity and respect. Our mission is directly tied to the humanity, dignity and inherent value of each employee, patient, community member and supporter. Our commitment to learning across our differences and similarities make us stronger. We seek employees who bring different and innovative ways of seeing the world and solving problems.
  
  
Fred Hutch Cancer Center is seeking a
**Software Development Engineer II**
to drive the Oncoscape platform, a production-grade system for cancer research.
  
  
You will build intuitive user interfaces, design scalable backend systems, and develop analytical methods for high-dimensional data - all while collaborating closely with researchers and clinicians to turn complex scientific questions into robust software and actionable insights. In this role, you will deliver high-impact software and directly contribute to computational oncology research, shaping the platform and the discoveries it enables.
  
  
This role involves building and owning full stack features from 0 to 1. The team has an evolving ecosystem including data processing pipelines, one-click deployments into AWS environments for clients, and a growing suite of integrations into various platforms.
  
  
This role will have the opportunity to work partially at our campus and remotely.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Own and evolve the platform end-to-end: drive design, architecture, and iteration of a production system supporting clinical and genomic research workflows.
* Build high-performance full-stack applications: develop intuitive, scalable interfaces and services using React and TypeScript, enabling exploration of complex, high-dimensional datasets.
* Architect data-intensive systems: design secure, scalable APIs and data models for clinical and genomic data using AWS, balancing performance across client and server layers.
* Bridge research and product: translate ambiguous scientific needs into well-defined product features, analytical tools, and user workflows.
* Shape technical and product direction: contribute to architectural decisions, roadmap prioritization, and overall platform strategy in a dynamic environment.
* Collaborate across disciplines: partner with researchers, clinicians, and engineers to ensure the platform delivers meaningful, actionable insights.

**Qualifications**
**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in computer science or equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Minimum of 3-6 years of directly related experience.
* 3+ years of experience building and shipping full-stack applications from zero to production, using React, TypeScript, and AWS.
* 3+ years designing and delivering scalable, cloud-based systems.
* Proven ability to own and architect end-to-end, data-intensive systems, making sound tradeoffs across frontend, backend, and data processing layers.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments, contributing to both technical architecture and product strategy.
* Experience working in cross-functional teams, translating complex scientific requirements into intuitive, production-grade software.
* Strong analytical abilities and problem-solving skills.
* Knowledge of relational databases and T-SQL.
* Solid understanding of Object-Oriented Programming concepts, data structures and algorithms.
* Understanding of specific programming languages.
* Other department-determined skills or experience may be required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with AWS Marketplace and deploying reproducible cloud applications across multiple tenants.
* Demonstrated expertise in high-dimensional data analysis, including dimensionality reduction techniques (e.g., UMAP, PaCMAP, t-SNE) in oncology or genomics contexts.
* Familiarity with modern genomics workflows and their application to precision oncology and clinical decision-making.
